content:
tom: Heads-up: rk7b-ptq bring-up flagged by nightly shadowbench. NDCG@10 -0.028 vs fp16 on anchor_mix_v3. Anyone on call?
maya: I'm here. What's the slice breakdown? overall or certain cohorts?
rachel: I pulled the CI plot. Core queries flat, but the "rare-entity" and "long-doc" cohorts have the drop. MRR stable.
kevin: Could be truncation differences during candidate scoring. Are we flattening passages differently in the PTQ harness?
zeynep: Also check tokenizer + sequence-concat logic. PTQ build used our legacy token-merge util which dedups whitespace differently. That impacted tokens in previous 3b run.
tom: Good point. The PTQ artifact shows `tokenizer_version: 0.13.2` while prod eval uses `0.15.1`.
maya: Ugh. We should run a tokenizer parity pass first. But let's not assume it's the only cause. We should also lock candidate-gen topk and passage-chunking (chunk_size + stride).
ci-bot: CI: nightly-shadow/anchor_mix_v3 queued comparing fp16 vs rk7b-ptq. Snapshot: ndcg10_delta=-0.028 (p=0.012). See job 5019.
rachel: Plan proposal:
- Step 1: Tokenizer parity (force 0.15.1 in PTQ eval)
- Step 2: Match candidate-gen (topk=10, chunk_size=512, stride=128)
- Step 3: Run batch size=1 + kvpack off to remove packing differences
- Step 4: Apply embed-per-dim-scale tweak as a last resort
Include seeds [11, 22, 33] and bootstrap CIs on query-cohort.
kevin: Add also a "document boundary" probe: does PTQ trimming drop the end-of-doc markers causing candidate rerank order changes? We had that bug in 2023.
zeynep: I'll run steps 1-2. Tom can do the KVpack/batch parity and embedding tests.
tom: Will do. Command for tokenizer parity run (small split):
```
python -m eval.rerank --model rk7b-ptq --anchors anchor_mix_v3 --tokenizer=0.15.1 --topk=10 --chunk_size=512 --stride=128 --seed 11 --metric ndcg@10
```
rachel: For significance use cluster-bootstrap at query level, report median delta and 95% CI. Also compute per-slice p-values (long-doc / rare-entity).
ci-bot: Jobs created: 5020 (ptq-tokenizer-parity), 5021 (ptq-candidate-parity), 5022 (ptq-kvpack-batch-check). ETA ~1.5h. Artifacts to s3://redwood-debug/rerank/1796664322/.
zeynep: Quick tip: add `--log-candidates` to capture top-20 per query for failing ones. Saves time when triaging.
maya: Also capture token diffs for a handful of queries. We should persist them as `token-diff-{queryid}.json` in the artifact bundle.
kevin: If tokenizer parity reduces but doesn't eliminate gap, next is embed-rescale. We did per-dim rescale in rk3b-experiment and it helped tail.
tom: Update: job 5020 finished 12m. Tokenizer parity removed ~0.018 of the gap, long-doc slice delta now -0.007. Artifacts: https://ci.internal/rerank/5020/artifacts.json
rachel: That pins tokenizer as major contributor. Remaining small loss might be candidate-gen or packing.
zeynep: I've started job 5021 with `--topk=10` and chunk params. Logging enabled.
ci-bot: Job 5021 finished. Candidate parity further reduced delta to -0.003; long-doc slice ~-0.002. Artifacts: s3://redwood-debug/rerank/1796664322/candidate_parity.json
maya: Looks like packing/kv is the last 3-4 points. Tom can you run kvpack=false + batch=1?
tom: On it. Job 5022 started.
kevin: If kvpack is culprit, we should patch PTQ runtime to preserve chunk boundaries or ensure hash-stable packing for eval. Also add an eval assertion that candidate tokens per-doc are identical across builds.
ci-bot: Job 5022 finished. With kvpack=false & batch=1 the delta is now within noise: ndcg10_delta=-0.0008 (p=0.44). Full report: https://ci.internal/rerank/5022/report.html
rachel: Great! So root causes: tokenizer drift (major) + candidate-chunking + packing heuristics (minor). Action items:
- Add tokenizer-parity gate to PTQ CI (fail if tokenizer mismatch)
- Standardize candidate-gen params in PTQ harness (topk/chunk/stride)
- Add eval-time assertion on candidate tokenization + top-k consistency
- Consider embed-rescale only if we reintroduce small variance later
maya: I'll open a PR for the tokenizer gate + candidate-gen lock. Tagging kevin & zeynep for review.
zeynep: I'll add `--log-candidates` to the PTQ regression run by default and persist diffs to S3.
kevin: For release notes, call this out as "PTQ bringup: tokenizer & chunking parity fix" and include slice metrics.
tom: Closing loop. Thanks team. Will follow up once PRs land. :rocket:
